sentences.text: CRIMINAL CASE No. 28556 of 2024  RAJESH KOLI  Versus
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 (SHRI AVINASH TRIVEDI, LEARNED COUNSEL FOR THE PETITIONER)
 (SHRI VINOD THAKUR, LEARNED GOVT. ADVOCATE APPEARING ON  BEHALF OF ADVOCATE GENERAL)
 ORDER 1.They
are heard.
Perused the case diary/challan papers.

2. This is the second application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, as he / she is implicated in connection with Crime No.811/2022 registered at Police Station-Manawar District-Dhar (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 343, 363, 366-A, 376,376(2)(n),
376(2)(k), 376(2)(f), 376(2)(i), 376(3),& 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 3/4,
5L, 5n & 6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 11.7.2022.

3. His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 6.1.2023 passed in MCRC.No.58910/2022.
4.
The allegation against the applicant is of abduction and rape.
5. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the prosecutrix has already been examined in the trial court and there are material omission and contradiction in her deposition.
It is also submitted that there is no chance that the applicant would interfere in trial any more.
Counsel for the applicant has submitted that out of 17 witnesses only two witnesses have been examined till now.
It is further submitted that the applicant is lodged in jail since 11.7.2022 and the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take a long time.
Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: 7.Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed the prayer.

8. Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the case diary, and that till now out of 17 witnesses only two witnesses have been examined and the fact that the applicant is lodged in jail since 11.7.2022 and the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take a long time., this Court is inclined to allow the application.
9. Accordingly, without reflecting anything on the merits of the case, the application filed by under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicant is hereby allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand)
with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he / she shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE das 3 MCRC-28556-2024 Rajesh Koli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96342975/
